description: Hand-curated core of the IE golden set: 10 parameters in increasing pipeline difficulty, from the standard-rate band (the happy path) to cases the current pipeline cannot solve by design (derived formula values, statistics-based parameters) so that future improvements show up as KPI deltas. Ireland has no OpenFisca package, so unlike FR there is no corpus drafter: expected values are hand-curated here from the acts themselves (Finance Act / Social Welfare Act quote them verbatim), drafted into cases by hand or via build-dataset over a trusted document, and every case stays verified:false until a human confirms it. See golden_set_IE.md for the full rationale per entry.

conventions.temporal_basis: All selected IE parameters are in_force: the Finance Act states values 'for the year of assessment 2025', which IS the EUROMOD system year — no FR-style income-year offset. Record this in an IE curation overlay rather than deriving it.
conventions.expected_value: Hand-curated ground truth (the LAW's value, cross-checked against the act text), since there is no OpenFisca corpus to read it from. Where it deliberately differs from EUROMOD's stored value the note says why. Percent literals ('4.1%') are kept in EUROMOD's spelling and normalise to the rate they denote (0.041). null means the value leg is not scored for this case.
conventions.routing: The routing a correct pipeline owes, which is the pipeline's own question: does the proposal differ from the value EUROMOD CURRENTLY HOLDS? It is not 'did the law change this year?'. The system-year N export already encodes the law of year N, so a parameter the legislature changed for N and that the export already carries routes `unchanged` — the pipeline's job there is to re-confirm it with a citation, and the difficulty of the case still lands on the value, citation and retrieval legs. Reserve `changed` for parameters where EUROMOD is genuinely stale relative to the law. Prefer leaving `routing:` out entirely and letting route_against_current decide; state it only where the stored value cannot be normalised (percent strings) or the case exists to pin a routing trap (derived, national_team_source). A stated routing that contradicts route_against_current SKIPS the entry — the drafter will not write ground truth it believes is wrong.
conventions.source: Every entry resolves through the parameter store via model_target; no entry reads a hand-authored parameter file. The IE export (old schema) has no groups block, so no assembled bracket-schedule case is possible — band and rate scalars stand in for the FR-style table case.

entries.note: EASY — the income-tax bracket case. Standard rate band, single person: 42,000 -> 44,000 for 2025, stated verbatim in Finance Act 2024 s. 3 (ingested, English, one section carries the whole PIT parameter set). The pipeline's happy path. ROUTING: EUROMOD already carries the 2025 value, so a correct pipeline routes `unchanged` — it must re-confirm the value with a citation, not propose a change. The 2024->2025 movement described above is still what the value and citation legs test.

EASY — no-change trap. Higher rate 40%, unchanged since 2015: Budget coverage revalorises the bands around it every year, so the pipeline must resist proposing a change it cannot cite. The provision is TCA 1997 s. 15 (not ingested — an instrument-level id of an act the corpus lacks is provenance, not ground truth); the citation is the ingested Finance Act 2024 s. 3, whose substituted Table restates 'The remainder | 40 per cent | the higher rate' for 2025.

EASY-MEDIUM — personal tax credit 1,875 -> 2,000 for 2025, in the same Finance Act section as the band: tests extracting several distinct parameters from one dense amending section without cross-contamination. ROUTING: EUROMOD already carries the 2025 value, so a correct pipeline routes `unchanged` — it must re-confirm the value with a citation, not propose a change. The 2024->2025 movement described above is still what the value and citation legs test.

MEDIUM — USC middle rate cut 4% -> 3% (Budget 2025). Stored numerically (0.03) so it scores cleanly, unlike the percent-string rates. USC lives in TCA Part 18D, amended by FA 2024 s. 2 — a different section than the PIT family. ROUTING: EUROMOD already carries the 2025 value, so a correct pipeline routes `unchanged` — it must re-confirm the value with a citation, not propose a change. The 2024->2025 movement described above is still what the value and citation legs test.

MEDIUM — USC 2% band ceiling. The law says 27,382 (12,012 + 15,370); EUROMOD stores 27,383 — a EUROMOD-side off-by-one, mirroring the FR bareme 1-euro erratum, to be reported to the economists team. Per the FR precedent the expected value is the LAW's (27,382), and the 1e-6 scoring tolerance keeps the difference visible.

MEDIUM-HARD — Jobseeker's Benefit graduated personal rate (earnings band 1), 109.50/week for 2025. The value sits in a rates SCHEDULE (table retrieval, not prose) of the annual Social Welfare Act amending SWCA 2005 Sch. 2, and the weekly basis (#w) exercises the x4.34 cross-period conversion the FR set barely touches. Pin the exact amending section when drafting. ROUTING: EUROMOD already carries the 2025 value, so a correct pipeline routes `unchanged` — it must re-confirm the value with a citation, not propose a change. The 2024->2025 movement described above is still what the value and citation legs test.

HARD — employee PRSI Class A. Two traps at once: (1) the value is stored as the percent string '4.1%' — EUROMOD's own spelling for a rate, which normalise_value now reads as 0.041 so it compares against the unit-/1 form the rest of the store uses; the expected value stays in EUROMOD's spelling on purpose; (2) the rate steps every 1 October (4.0 -> 4.1 on 2024-10-01, -> 4.2 on 2025-10-01, per the Social Welfare (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2024 roadmap), so 'the 2025 value' is ambiguous between the value in force at as_of (4.1%), the post-October value (4.2%), and a FYA weighted average — exactly the ambiguity route_against_current refuses to draft, hence the explicit routing. ROUTING: EUROMOD already holds '4.1%', so a correct pipeline routes `unchanged` — and must not propose a bare 4.1, which is a hundredfold different rate.

HARD / not_found today — the Budget 2025 electricity credit (2 x 125). Set by the one-off Electricity Costs (Domestic Electricity Accounts) Emergency Measures Acts, which are NOT among the 15 ingested IE acts, so the case measures ingest breadth + the scout gap-fill (IE was added to scout.COUNTRY_SOURCES for exactly this). Citations left empty until the act is ingested — an instrument-level citation of an act we do not hold is provenance, not ground truth. Verify the exact 2024/2025 act title and the per-credit vs annual amount when drafting. ROUTING: EUROMOD already carries the 2025 value, so a correct pipeline routes `unchanged` — it must re-confirm the value with a citation, not propose a change. The 2024->2025 movement described above is still what the value and citation legs test.

IMPOSSIBLE today, by design — Child Benefit stored as '140#m*$sw_weeks'. The $sw_weeks reference makes pipeline._derived_refs short-circuit to routing 'derived' before any retrieval, even though the legislated 140/month sits plainly in SWCA 2005 Sch. 4. Expected routing pins today's correct contract behaviour; the future improvement (resolve the anchor, retrieve and propose on the monthly amount, then recompose) flips this case's expectation to a scored value. Also exposes the scoring bug where normalise_value truncates the expression at '#'. Value deliberately not scored until then.

IMPOSSIBLE forever — an implicit consumption-tax rate derived from Household Budget Survey statistics, with no legislative source at all (stands for the whole 268-parameter tco_ie family). The correct behaviour is a national_team_source refusal, which requires creating curation/IE.curation.yaml (none exists yet) with a source_type: national_team block, mirroring LT's xcc_lt precedent. The FR set has zero such traps; this one tests that the pipeline routes around non-legislative parameters instead of reporting not_found every run.

DERIVE, and the only one Ireland has — the taper rate of the PRSI Class A credit. The law states the reduction in words, 'one-sixth of the amount by which weekly earnings exceed the threshold', and EUROMOD stores the arithmetic '1/6'; a correct proposal has to turn the words into the fraction, which is the whole point of the rung. corpus_available: false — the tapered credit was introduced in 2016 and lives in an amendment to SWCA 2005 s.13, while the ingested consolidation carries only the original version (validity ends 2022-01-01, no mention of a credit or of the EUR 352.01 threshold). Ingesting the amending Social Welfare Act is what turns this case from a coverage measure into a quality one; until then it belongs in the no_corpus slice.
